nodes.name: Start-up and providers
nodes.summary: How the single-page app boots: runtime configuration, the provider tree, error tracking, analytics and the lazy section routes.
nodes.detail: Vite builds src/index.tsx into one page whose index.html carries window.__SALEOR_CONFIG__ (the API address, mount path, extension and cloud addresses). At load the entry point starts Google Tag Manager when a tag is configured, initialises Sentry error tracking, then renders the App component: about twenty nested React providers (Apollo, router, themes, locale, notifications, background tasks, app state, auth, analytics, shop, channel, forms, dev mode, command menu, save bar, feature flags, onboarding). Routes decide between the sign-in screen, a 'cannot reach the API' view, a loader and the signed-in layout with one lazy-loaded route per section.

nodes.name: Routing and permission gates
nodes.summary: React Router v5 history with the mount path as basename, routes that check the staff member's permissions, and redirects for legacy paths.
nodes.detail: A browser history is created with getAppMountUri() as basename and every Route is wrapped for Sentry tracing. SectionRoute reads the signed-in user and renders the section only when the user holds all (or, with matchPermission any, one) of the listed PermissionEnum codes; otherwise it renders the not-found page. RootRoutes keeps the set-new-password page reachable whatever the session state, and RequirePermissions hides pieces of a page the same way.

nodes.name: Apollo GraphQL client
nodes.summary: The one Apollo client every screen uses, its link chain to the GraphQL endpoint, token handling in the fetch, the schema-aware cache and the generated hooks.
nodes.detail: client.ts builds an ApolloClient whose link is attachVariablesLink (adds an optional source-service-name header and copies variables into each result) followed by apollo-upload-client's upload link (multipart file uploads, credentials included). Its fetch is createFetch from authFetch.ts, which adds the access token as the authorization-bearer header, refreshes the JSON Web Token (JWT) before it expires and retries once on ExpiredSignatureError; trackConnection wraps it to report outages. The cache is an InMemoryCache subclass that strips fields locked to the other schema version. There is no batch link: every operation is its own POST. Typed hooks come from GraphQL Code Generator; makeQuery and makeMutation wrap them with error notifications and permission variables.

nodes.name: Sign-in and session
nodes.summary: Email and password sign-in, external OpenID Connect sign-in, token storage and refresh, the user context and the sign-in screens.
nodes.detail: initAuth wires a small authentication software development kit (SDK) onto the shared Apollo client and, when a refresh token is stored in localStorage, refreshes it at boot (autologin) with retries and a 15 second timeout. useAuthProvider exposes login, external login, logout and the current user (the UserDetails query) through UserContext; it rejects users without permissions or who are not staff. Session flags (authenticated, authenticating, isStaff, API unreachable) live in Apollo reactive variables, not in the cache. The access token is kept only in memory; the refresh token and auth plugin id are kept in localStorage.

nodes.name: Connection monitoring
nodes.summary: Notices when the Saleor API stops answering, shows a banner, probes until it answers again and reloads the queries that failed meanwhile.
nodes.detail: trackConnection wraps the Apollo fetch and reports every response or network failure to a connection monitor state machine (online, suspect, offline, unreachable, restored). While in an outage the monitor probes the API with a bare '__typename' query outside Apollo, so the probe never refreshes tokens or touches the cache. ConnectionRecovery and the banner react to the state, and failedQueryRecovery refetches queries that failed during the outage. Lazy section bundles that fail to download (connection lost or a new release) get their own error page rather than a crash report.

nodes.name: Feature flags
nodes.summary: Feature flags defined as markdown files, resolved at runtime from localStorage, build-time FF_ environment variables and the staff member's metadata.
nodes.detail: scripts/build-flags.cjs turns the .featureFlags/*.md front matter into a generated list of flags with defaults and descriptions. FeatureFlagsProviderWithUser builds three strategies (localStorage, the FF_ environment variables Vite injects as the FLAGS global, and the user's 'feature_flags' metadata key), a FlagsResolver fetches all of them and combines them by priority, and the app shows a loader until flags resolve. useFlag reads one flag; a sidebar modal lets a staff member toggle visible flags and saves them to their metadata through accountUpdate.

nodes.name: Layout and navigation
nodes.summary: The signed-in frame: sidebar menu filtered by permissions, top navigation, channel picker, navigation pins, announcements, ripples, dev mode panel and the save bar anchor.
nodes.detail: AppLayout renders the sidebar, the command menu, the GraphQL dev mode panel, the connection banner, store announcements and the sticky save bar anchor around the routed page. The sidebar menu (useMenuStructure) lists sections with the permissions each needs and splices in app extensions mounted at NAVIGATION_* points; navigation pins add shortcuts to filtered model lists, stored in user and shop public metadata. AppChannelContext keeps the selected channel in localStorage and falls back to the first channel the user can access.

nodes.name: Global search and command menu
nodes.summary: The Ctrl or Cmd+K command menu with quick actions and resource search, and the full search page that queries several entity types at once.
nodes.detail: NavigatorSearch opens a modal on ctrl+k or meta+k; CommandContent lists navigation actions, app search actions and resources found by the NavigatorSearch query (two of each of orders, categories, collections, products, variants, models and model types). The /search section runs the GlobalSearch query with @include flags chosen from the user's permissions, keeps search history, and shows up to ten results per type (five for model types). The searches folder holds the paginated search hooks every picker dialog uses.

nodes.name: Home page
nodes.summary: The /home page, built entirely from app extensions mounted at HOMEPAGE_WIDGETS, plus the onboarding checklist and welcome sidebar.
nodes.detail: HomePage loads the extensions mounted at HOMEPAGE_WIDGETS, filters them by the user's permissions, splits them into full-screen tabs and a widgets grid, applies the staff member's hide and pin preferences and redirects /home to the leftmost tab. One Route covers /home, /home/widget/:extensionId and /home/widgets so keep-alive iframes stay mounted across tab changes. With no extensions it shows an empty state that promotes the Pulse app. The welcomePage folder holds the onboarding checklist whose state is saved in user metadata.

nodes.name: Shared components
nodes.summary: The building blocks every section uses: the data grid, conditional filters, forms and save bar, notifications, dialogs, attribute editors, channel availability and tables.
nodes.detail: Sections compose their list and detail pages from these components rather than from raw Macaw UI. Lists use the Glide data grid with persisted columns and the conditional filter bar that syncs filters to the address bar and builds GraphQL where or filter variables. Detail pages use the Form and Savebar components with an exit-without-saving guard, the attribute and metadata editors, and assign dialogs for picking products, variants, categories and more.

nodes.name: Shared hooks and utilities
nodes.summary: Hooks and helpers for navigation, list settings, pagination, bulk selection, local storage, error messages, mutation handlers and address building.
nodes.detail: useNavigator wraps history pushes, useListSettings and useLocalStorage persist per-list page size and columns in localStorage, usePaginator and useLocalPaginator turn cursor page info into next and previous links, and useBulkActions and useRowSelection track selected rows. utils/errors maps every API error code to a translated message, utils/handlers builds the change handlers forms use, and misc.ts extracts mutation errors and statuses.

nodes.name: Build, deploy and tooling
nodes.summary: Package scripts, GraphQL code generation, the Docker and nginx image, static-host configs and release scripts.
nodes.detail: package.json pins pnpm and Node 24 and runs code generation before dev and build. Two GraphQL Code Generator configs produce types, hooks, fragment matchers and type policies from schema-main.graphql and schema-staging.graphql. The Dockerfile builds with Vite in a Node 24 Alpine stage and serves build/dashboard from nginx, whose entrypoint script rewrites window.__SALEOR_CONFIG__ values in index.html from environment variables at container start. Netlify, Heroku and static-host configs route every path to index.html.

nodes.name: Docs and agent guides
nodes.summary: The README, the glossary, agent instructions, architecture decision records and the configuration, deployment and multi-schema guides.
nodes.detail: AGENTS.md sets the conventions (Macaw UI next, CSS Modules, strict TypeScript, react-intl, code generation after GraphQL changes). CONTEXT.md is the glossary of dashboard names that differ from API names (Model is Page, Model type is PageType). Two architecture decision records cover navigation pin storage in public metadata and Saleor Cloud features in a private submodule. docs/ explains environment variables, Docker, deployment, error tracking and the main and staging schema build.

nodes.name: Dashboard entry point
nodes.summary: Mounts the React app on #dashboard-app, initialises Google Tag Manager and Sentry, and declares the provider tree and the section routes.
nodes.detail: Module-level side effects run first: TagManager.initialize when GTM_ID is set, errorTracker.init(history), and a legacy theme migration from the activeMacawUITheme localStorage key. Twenty-nine page sections and route components are React.lazy imports so each becomes its own bundle. React StrictMode wraps the app only in development unless VITE_DISABLE_STRICT_MODE is true.
facts: StrictMode only when import.meta.env.DEV and VITE_DISABLE_STRICT_MODE is not 'true'
/ redirects to /home; /apps, /custom-apps/ and /plugins redirect to the installed extensions list

nodes.name: App provider tree
nodes.summary: Nests the Apollo, router, theme, locale, notification, auth, shop, channel and feature-flag providers around the routes.
nodes.detail: Order matters: AuthProvider sits inside NotificationProvider so sign-in errors can toast, ShopProvider and AppChannelProvider sit inside AuthProvider because they skip their queries until the user is signed in, and FeatureFlagsProviderWithUser sits low because one strategy reads the user's metadata. NotificationsToaster and ConnectionRecovery render beside the routes under the save bar provider so toasts clear the sticky save bar.
nodes.code:
const App = (): React.ReactNode => (
  <ApolloProvider client={apolloClient}>
    <Router>
      {/* @ts-expect-error legacy types */}
      <LegacyThemeProvider overrides={themeOverrides} palettes={paletteOverrides}>
        <ThemeProvider>
          <LocaleProvider>
            <NotificationProvider>
              <BackgroundTasksProvider>
                <AppStateProvider>
                  <AuthProvider>
                    <ProductAnalytics>
                      <ShopProvider>
                        <TranslationLocalesProvider>
                          <AppChannelProvider>

nodes.name: Routes()
nodes.summary: Chooses between the signed-in layout, the API-unreachable view, a loader and the sign-in screens, then switches between section routes.
nodes.detail: The signed-in branch requires both authentication and a resolved channel. It wraps the sections in AppExtensionPopupProvider, StaffInviteProvider, AppLayout and an ErrorBoundary that reports to Sentry and shows an error page, except for failed lazy-bundle downloads, which get the section load error view. Each section is a SectionRoute with the PermissionEnum codes it needs; extensions use an empty list, and /staff and /taxes declare none.

nodes.name: Runtime configuration
nodes.summary: Reads API, mount, static, cloud and extensions addresses from window.__SALEOR_CONFIG__ and holds default list settings and page sizes.
nodes.detail: getApiUrl returns window.__SALEOR_CONFIG__.API_URL, which may be relative; getAbsoluteApiUrl resolves it against the page origin for apps and new-tab extensions. The file also holds the default columns and row counts for every list view, notification display times and the ENABLED_SERVICE_NAME_HEADER switch read by the Apollo link.
facts: SW_INTERVAL defaults to 300 but nothing reads it
APP_VERSION comes from CUSTOM_VERSION or package.json version

nodes.name: HTML shell and runtime config
nodes.summary: The page template: the #dashboard-app root, portals for modals and toasts, and the window.__SALEOR_CONFIG__ object filled at build or container start.

nodes.name: Vite build configuration
nodes.summary: Exposes a fixed list of environment variables to the bundle, injects FF_ variables as the FLAGS global and builds into build/dashboard.
nodes.detail: Only named variables reach process.env in the bundle (API_URL, SENTRY_DSN, POSTHOG_KEY, FF_USE_STAGING_SCHEMA and others); every variable starting with FF_ is serialised into the FLAGS global. The HTML plugin templates index.html with the runtime config, the Sentry plugin uploads source maps when SENTRY_AUTH_TOKEN is set, and the dev server listens on PORT, PORT_DEVSERVER or 9000.

nodes.name: App state and background tasks
nodes.summary: A reducer for the global loader and error state, and a provider that polls export and invoice jobs every 15 seconds until they finish.
nodes.detail: AppStateProvider holds loading and error flags that makeQuery's displayLoader and the root error boundary dispatch to. BackgroundTasksProvider keeps a queue of tasks in a ref; one setInterval of 15 000 ms queries CheckExportFileStatus or CheckOrderInvoicesStatus for each pending task and notifies when the job succeeds or fails.

nodes.name: Locale and translations
nodes.summary: Uses the language saved in localStorage, else LOCALE_CODE (default EN), loads its react-intl message file and provides it to the app.
nodes.detail: LocaleProvider reads the locale localStorage key, falls back to LOCALE_CODE, lazily imports the matching JSON file from locale/ for any language other than English and renders IntlProvider keyed by locale. src/intl.ts holds shared messages such as section names and common errors.

nodes.name: Error tracking
nodes.summary: A tracker interface with a Sentry adapter: initialises Sentry with router tracing when SENTRY_DSN is set and tags events with the API host.
nodes.detail: ErrorTrackerFactory wraps an adapter so the app calls init, captureException and setUserData without knowing the vendor. The Sentry adapter ignores three noisy browser and editor errors, samples 10 percent of traces and sets the user name to the API hostname so events group per store.

nodes.name: Product analytics
nodes.summary: Wraps the app in a PostHog provider when POSTHOG_KEY is set, with page views and autocapture off and addresses sanitised before sending.
nodes.detail: The before_send hook rewrites seven URL properties through sanitizeAnalyticsUrl so identifiers in paths do not leave the browser. ShopProvider initialises analytics with the shop domain, the staff member's email domain and the dashboard and Saleor versions; useAnalytics exposes trackEvent to features such as extension installation.

nodes.name: Shop provider
nodes.summary: Runs the ShopInfo query once the user is signed in and shares the shop (countries, domain, version, limits) through context.
nodes.detail: The ShopInfo query is skipped until the user is authenticated. When both the shop and the user are known, it initialises product analytics with the shop domain, the staff member's email domain and the dashboard and Saleor versions. useShop reads the context elsewhere, for example for the core version sent to apps.

nodes.name: Router and history
nodes.summary: Creates the browser history with the mount path as basename and exports a Sentry-instrumented Route.
nodes.detail: history is created once at module load with basename getAppMountUri(), so the app can live under /dashboard/ or any other mount path. Route is Sentry.withSentryRouting(BaseRoute), which names transactions after route patterns for tracing. useRouteChange lets components react to path or query changes.

nodes.name: SectionRoute
nodes.summary: A Route that renders its section only when the signed-in user holds all, or any, of the listed permissions; otherwise the not-found page.
nodes.detail: It returns nothing while the user is still undefined to avoid a race with the UserDetails query. With no permissions prop it always renders; an empty list also passes because Array.every on an empty list is true. The default match is all.

nodes.name: Permission checks
nodes.summary: hasPermission, hasAnyPermissions and hasAllPermissions compare PermissionEnum codes against the user's userPermissions.

nodes.name: RequirePermissions
nodes.summary: Renders its children only when the user has all requiredPermissions or one of oneOfPermissions; used inside pages for buttons and cards.

nodes.name: Routes outside the auth gate
nodes.summary: Keeps the set-new-password route reachable whether or not someone is signed in, then falls through to the gated content.
nodes.detail: An OpenID Connect user can be signed in and still need to set a password, so the new-password page cannot live only behind the sign-in gate.

nodes.name: Apollo client setup
nodes.summary: Builds the single ApolloClient: the header and variables link, the upload link with authenticated fetch, and the schema-aware cache with type policies.
nodes.detail: The upload link points at getApiUrl() with credentials included and a fetch made of createFetch wrapped by trackConnection. Type policies key CountryDisplay by code, treat Shop as a singleton, disable merging for Money, TaxedMoney, Weight and User.addresses, fall back to the name for empty AttributeValue slugs and disable normalisation for App. The same module calls initAuth so authentication shares this client and cache.
facts: Header source-service-name: saleor.dashboard when ENABLED_SERVICE_NAME_HEADER is 'true'
No batch link: one HTTP POST per operation

nodes.name: attachVariablesLink
nodes.summary: Apollo link that adds the optional service-name header and copies the operation variables into each result's extensions.

nodes.name: SchemaAwareCache
nodes.summary: InMemoryCache subclass whose transformDocument strips @lockSchema fields for the other schema version before cache and link see the query.
nodes.detail: Doing it in the cache rather than a link keeps cache normalisation and the outgoing request in step; a link-level transform would leave the cache expecting fields the API was never asked for.

nodes.name: apolloClient
nodes.summary: The exported ApolloClient instance that ApolloProvider, the auth SDK and the background task poller share.

nodes.name: Authenticated fetch
nodes.summary: The fetch the Apollo link uses: adds the access token, refreshes it before expiry or on ExpiredSignatureError and retries once, with one shared refresh.
nodes.detail: Refresh requests themselves (RefreshToken, RefreshTokenWithUser, ExternalRefresh, ExternalRefreshWithUser) pass straight through. Other requests decode the JSON Web Token (JWT) and refresh when it expires within 120 seconds; the token owner 'saleor' picks tokenRefresh, anything else externalRefresh. A session id guards against a logout or another sign-in while a request waited: such requests throw SessionEndedError or SessionExpiredError instead of answering for the new session. A failed refresh caused by the network surfaces as a transient error rather than a logout.
facts: Retry on ExpiredSignatureError once, with refresh disabled on the retry

nodes.name: runTokenRefresh()
nodes.summary: Single-flight token refresh: concurrent requests in the same session await one refresh promise instead of each sending its own.
nodes.detail: When a sleeping tab wakes, Apollo replays every active query at once with the same expired token; without coalescing each would refresh and invalidate the others' tokens. Only the caller that started the refresh clears the shared promise.

nodes.name: createFetch()
nodes.summary: Returns a fetch that attaches the authorization-bearer header, refreshes near expiry and retries a request the API rejected as expired.
nodes.detail: Proxy error pages that are not JSON are passed on unchanged so Apollo can report the HTTP status as a connection failure. On a refreshed token it calls itself with autoTokenRefresh and refreshOnUnauthorized both false, so a request is retried at most once.
nodes.signature: createFetch({ autoTokenRefresh = true, tokenRefreshTimeSkew = 120, refreshOnUnauthorized = true } = {}) => (input, init) => Promise<Response>

nodes.name: @lockSchema resolver
nodes.summary: Removes fields marked @lockSchema for the schema version not being built, and strips the directive so it never reaches the API.
nodes.detail: The dashboard is compiled against a main and a staging Saleor schema. A plain graphql visitor drops locked selections; an operation locked entirely to the other version cannot be stripped, so callers gate it by hand.

nodes.name: Generated hooks and types
nodes.summary: GraphQL Code Generator output: typed Apollo hooks, operation types, fragment matchers and type policies for the main and staging schemas.
nodes.detail: Never hand-edited; regenerated by pnpm run generate from every queries.ts, mutations.ts and fragments file. index.ts re-exports the main-schema hooks and types.

nodes.name: Shared GraphQL fragments
nodes.summary: Thirty-one fragment files (User, App, Order, Product, errors and more) reused across every query and mutation.
nodes.detail: The App fragment includes accessToken, so every app details query also returns the app's JSON Web Token for its iframe.

nodes.name: Query hook wrapper
nodes.summary: useQuery around Apollo's: injects PERMISSION_* variables, uses cache-and-network by default, drives the global loader and turns errors into notifications.
nodes.detail: makeQuery(document) returns a hook bound to that document, which generated hooks build on. The wrapper adds permission variables, defaults fetchPolicy to cache-and-network with errorPolicy all, optionally drives the global loader and adds loadMore, a fetchMore helper that merges pages with a caller-supplied function.

nodes.name: useQuery()
nodes.summary: Adds a boolean variable per permission to every query, sets errorPolicy all, and routes errors to session, connection or authorisation handlers.
nodes.detail: Every PermissionEnum code becomes a PERMISSION_<code> variable, true when the user holds it, so queries can @include permission-gated fields. Session-ended errors are silent, session-expired errors toast, connection errors toast only when no connection banner is attached, and other errors go to handleQueryAuthError. It also passes context useBatching: true, which no link reads.
nodes.signature: useQuery<TData, TVariables>(query: DocumentNode, opts?: QueryHookOptions) => UseQueryResult

nodes.name: Mutation hook wrapper
nodes.summary: useMutation around Apollo's: reports nested errors from the payload, read-only and expired-session errors, and connection failures as toasts.
nodes.detail: On completion it runs handleNestedMutationErrors so errors arrays inside the mutation payload become notifications. On error it toasts read-only mode, logs out on JSON Web Token (JWT) errors, does not toast LimitReachedException and, for connection failures, warns without claiming nothing was saved, since a timed-out create may have reached the API.

nodes.name: Auth bootstrap and autologin
nodes.summary: Creates token storage and the auth SDK on the Apollo client, registers it with the authenticated fetch and refreshes a stored session at boot.
nodes.detail: If a refresh token is stored, authenticating is set immediately so the sign-in screen never flashes. The boot refresh races a 15 second timeout and is retried after 1 and 3 seconds when the failure is transient (offline, 502, 503); if it still fails the app shows the API-unreachable view but keeps the refresh token. A refresh that times out is never sent twice with the same token, because a single sign-on provider that rotates tokens could treat it as reuse.

nodes.name: autologin()
nodes.summary: Refreshes the stored session at start-up, retrying transient failures and flagging the API as unreachable when they persist.
nodes.signature: const autologin = async (authSdk: AuthSDK, refreshToken: string): Promise<void>

nodes.name: Auth SDK
nodes.summary: Login, logout, token refresh, set password and external OpenID Connect calls as Apollo mutations that write tokens and session state.
nodes.detail: login seeds the UserDetails cache entry from tokenCreate's user so signing in costs one request. Refreshes use fetchPolicy no-cache and ignore results that arrive after the session changed; a refresh without a token logs out. External sign-in stores the auth plugin id and accepts the tokens only when the user has at least one permission. logout clears storage, resets state, calls clearStore (not resetStore, which would refetch every query without a token) and, for an external session, asks the plugin for a logout address.

nodes.name: auth()
nodes.summary: Factory returning the AuthSDK object bound to the shared Apollo client; login stores both tokens and marks the session authenticated.

nodes.name: Token storage
nodes.summary: Keeps the access token in memory and the refresh token and auth plugin id in localStorage, with a session id that changes on every sign-in or logout.
facts: Token owner 'saleor' marks an internal token; others are external

nodes.name: Session state
nodes.summary: Apollo reactive variables for authenticated, authenticating and isStaff, plus API unreachable and another-account-chosen flags.
nodes.detail: Kept out of the Apollo cache on purpose: the old vendored SDK stored them as client fields on Query, which forced the User type to be a singleton, a storefront assumption that broke staff and customer lists.

nodes.name: User context provider
nodes.summary: Builds the UserContext value: login, external login, logout, the current user from UserDetails and translated sign-in errors.
nodes.detail: UserDetails runs cache-first once authenticated, reading the user that login seeded. When no session exists and the API is reachable it tries the browser Credential Management API once to sign in with saved credentials. authenticated is exposed only when the token is valid, the user is staff and there are no errors.

nodes.name: useAuthProvider()
nodes.summary: Signs in with email and password, logs out users with no permissions or who are not staff, and maps account error codes to messages.

nodes.name: Auth GraphQL operations
nodes.summary: GraphQL documents for tokenCreate, tokenRefresh, the external authentication mutations, setPassword and requestPasswordReset.
nodes.detail: The WithUser refresh variants ask only for the minimal AuthUser fragment, because only tokenCreate makes the request authenticated for field resolution; asking for permission-guarded fields would fail the whole mutation.

nodes.name: Sign-in view
nodes.summary: Shows email and password and the configured external providers, starts the OpenID Connect redirect and completes it on the callback.
nodes.detail: It queries AvailableExternalAuthentications for the providers and the password login mode. Choosing a provider asks externalAuthenticationUrl for an authorization address with the callback path as redirect, remembers the plugin and the current page, and sends the browser away. On return, code and state are exchanged once (a module-level guard stops StrictMode and remounts from spending the single-use code twice), then the user is sent back to the remembered page.

nodes.name: Sign-in page UI
nodes.summary: The email and password form, external provider buttons, last-used-method hint and error messages.

nodes.name: Password reset screens
nodes.summary: Request a reset email, confirm it was sent, and set a new password from the emailed token, which also signs the user in.

nodes.name: Auth and session errors
nodes.summary: Error classes for ended and expired sessions and timeouts, transient request detection and parsing of sign-in errors.
nodes.detail: SessionEndedError marks a request that belonged to a session that was logged out or replaced; SessionExpiredError marks one whose refresh token the API refused. Transient errors (offline, timeouts, 502 and 503) are recognised so a failed refresh is not mistaken for a logout. parseAuthError maps GraphQL errors from sign-in to user-facing error codes.

nodes.name: API unreachable view
nodes.summary: Shown when the boot-time session refresh cannot reach Saleor: retry the stored session or sign in with another account.

nodes.name: Saved browser credentials
nodes.summary: Uses the browser Credential Management API to save the password after sign-in and to sign in silently when credentials exist.
nodes.detail: After a successful password sign-in the email and password are stored with navigator.credentials.store. On a later visit with no session, useAuthProvider asks navigator.credentials.get for a password credential and signs in with it once. Logout calls preventSilentAccess only when credentials exist, because Chrome 115 crashed otherwise.

nodes.name: Auth redirection
nodes.summary: Tells the routes whether the user is authenticated or still authenticating, so the shell can pick the screen.

nodes.name: Connection monitor
nodes.summary: State machine that turns request outcomes into online, suspect, offline, unreachable and restored states and schedules probes.
nodes.detail: A failed request moves the state to suspect and schedules a check, so one dropped request does not flash a banner. A failed check sets offline when the browser has no network, otherwise unreachable, and checks repeat with growing delays, random jitter and any Retry-After the API sent, skipping automatic checks while the page is hidden. The first successful check moves to restored, shown briefly before online, and emits lost, restored and recovered events that the banner, analytics and query recovery listen to.

nodes.name: trackConnection()
nodes.summary: Wraps the Apollo fetch and reports each network failure or failing HTTP status to the monitor, passing the request through unchanged.

nodes.name: Connection probe
nodes.summary: Posts 'query ConnectionCheck { __typename }' to the API outside Apollo with a 10 second timeout; any answer means Saleor is reachable.

nodes.name: Failed query recovery
nodes.summary: Remembers queries that failed during an outage and refetches them once the connection is restored.
nodes.detail: When Saleor answers again it walks Apollo's active queries and refetches only those whose last error was a connection error. Queries that loaded fine are left alone so forms are not reset, queries still loading are skipped, and mutations are never repeated. After a single failed request each query is retried once; one that keeps failing while the API answers is counted so the staff member can be told.

nodes.name: Connection banner and recovery
nodes.summary: The sticky banner shown during an outage, the component that reloads data when the API answers again, and the section download error page.

nodes.name: Feature flags provider
nodes.summary: Resolves flags from localStorage, environment and user metadata strategies and blocks rendering with a loader until they are known.

nodes.name: Flag strategies
nodes.summary: Where flag values come from: localStorage, the FLAGS build global, the user's feature_flags metadata key and the generated defaults.
nodes.detail: Each strategy implements fetchAll() and returns a full flag list. LocalStorageStrategy reads overrides saved in the browser, EnvVarsStrategy extends ObjectStorageStrategy over the FLAGS global built from FF_ variables, and MetadataStrategy parses the 'feature_flags' metadata entry and falls back to the generated defaults for flags it does not mention.

nodes.name: useFlag()
nodes.summary: Reads one flag's enabled state and payload from the flags context.

nodes.name: Flag definitions generator
nodes.summary: Reads .featureFlags/*.md front matter and markdown bodies and writes the generated AVAILABLE_FLAGS module with rendered descriptions.

nodes.name: Feature flags modal
nodes.summary: A modal in the user menu that lists visible flags, lets a staff member toggle them and saves the choice to their metadata.

nodes.name: App layout
nodes.summary: The signed-in frame: sidebar, command menu, dev mode panel, connection banner, announcements, the routed page and the save bar anchor.
nodes.detail: A linear progress bar shows while app state says loading. The fullSize prop is declared and passed from the routes but never read.

nodes.name: Sidebar
nodes.summary: The collapsible navigation rail or drawer with the section menu, shortcuts, user controls and the deprecation banner.

nodes.name: Sidebar menu structure
nodes.summary: Builds the menu tree with the permissions each section needs and adds app extensions mounted at the NAVIGATION_* points.

nodes.name: Selected channel context
nodes.summary: Stores the chosen channel id in localStorage and resets it to the first channel the user can access when it is no longer valid.
nodes.detail: The selected channel id lives in the 'channel' localStorage key. When it is missing or not in the user's accessibleChannels it is reset to the first accessible channel. The provider also lists the channels for the picker; the routes wait for a channel before rendering the signed-in layout.

nodes.name: Navigation pins
nodes.summary: Sidebar shortcuts to model lists filtered by one model type: user pins in the staff member's metadata, organization pins in shop metadata.
nodes.detail: Both are one JSON value in public metadata, as decided in architecture decision record 0001. User pins arrive with UserDetails; organization pins have their own ShopNavigationPins query with a localStorage snapshot for the first paint. Writing organization pins needs MANAGE_SETTINGS. Pinned model type names are fetched by a query built at runtime with one aliased field per pin.

nodes.name: Store announcements
nodes.summary: Reads shop announcements from the API and shows them above the page, grouped by severity.
nodes.detail: useAnnouncements runs the Announcements query on the shop, mappers turn the API objects into view models and groupBySeverity orders them so the most severe show first. AnnouncementsContainer renders them at the top of every page inside the layout.

nodes.name: Ripples
nodes.summary: Small animated markers next to changed parts of the interface that a staff member acknowledges once; seen state is kept in localStorage.
nodes.detail: Each ripple has an id and a time to live. RipplesStorage keeps, per ripple, when it was first seen and whether it was hidden, in the 'dashboard-ripples' localStorage key through a jotai atom, and hides a ripple once its time to live has passed or the staff member dismissed it. An all-ripples modal lists recent ones.

nodes.name: GraphQL dev mode panel
nodes.summary: A GraphiQL playground opened with Cmd or Ctrl+' that sends queries to the API with the staff member's token.
nodes.detail: The fetcher uses createFetch, so the playground benefits from token refresh, unless the user typed their own Authorization headers, in which case plain fetch is used. It sends source-service-name saleor.dashboard.playground when the service header is enabled and marks the onboarding step done on the first non-introspection query.

nodes.name: Saleor Cloud extension slot
nodes.summary: Lazy-loads the environment switcher from a private Git submodule when present and renders nothing when it is absent.
nodes.detail: import.meta.glob matches ./src/index.ts only when the submodule is checked out, so open-source builds compile and run without it, as architecture decision record 0002 describes.

nodes.name: Command menu
nodes.summary: Toggles a modal on ctrl+k or meta+k that lists actions and resource results with keyboard navigation.

nodes.name: Command menu resource results
nodes.summary: Runs the NavigatorSearch query, which asks for two of each entity type matching the typed text.

nodes.name: Command menu actions
nodes.summary: Lists the quick actions for the typed text, including actions contributed by apps through SEARCH_ACTION extensions and copy-id actions.

nodes.name: Search page
nodes.summary: The /search section: GlobalSearch over orders, products, variants, categories, collections, models and model types with history.
nodes.detail: useInclusionVariables turns the user's permissions and the chosen scope into @include flags, so the API is asked only for entity types the user may see. Results are flattened by prepareResults into one keyboard-navigable list.

nodes.name: Picker search hooks
nodes.summary: Paginated search hooks for products, variants, categories, collections, customers, warehouses and more, used by assign dialogs and comboboxes.
nodes.detail: Each hook wraps a search query with makeSearch or makeTopLevelSearch, which handle the search text, cursor pagination and loadMore for infinite scrolling. Assign dialogs, comboboxes and filters reuse them. makeSearch does not strip the PERMISSION_* variables the way makeQuery adds them.

nodes.name: Home page
nodes.summary: Loads HOMEPAGE_WIDGETS extensions, applies permission filters and preferences, and renders tabs of full-screen apps and a widget grid.
nodes.detail: While extensions load and no non-empty snapshot exists it renders a blank box, so the empty state never doubles as a placeholder. Stale or bare /home addresses redirect to the leftmost tab while still rendering the tab panels, so keep-alive iframes are not unmounted.

nodes.name: Home extension filter
nodes.summary: Keeps home extensions whose permissions the user holds and splits them into full-screen and widget targets.

nodes.name: Home tab panels
nodes.summary: Keeps every visited full-screen app iframe mounted and hidden when inactive, and shows the widgets grid tab.

nodes.name: Onboarding and welcome widgets
nodes.summary: The onboarding checklist and welcome sidebar (activities, sales and stock analytics); checklist state is saved in user metadata.
nodes.detail: OnboardingProvider keeps which onboarding steps are done and expanded and saves them with the SaveOnBoardingState mutation (updateMetadata on the user). Steps are marked done from elsewhere, for example by the GraphQL playground on its first query. The welcome sidebar queries recent activities, sales analytics and out-of-stock products for the selected channel.

nodes.name: Data grid
nodes.summary: The Glide data grid wrapper used by every list and by editable line tables, with custom cells, a column picker and persisted columns.
nodes.detail: Datagrid wraps @glideapps/glide-data-grid with row actions, row anchors that make rows real links, full-screen mode, tooltips and a change tracker for editable cells. Custom cells draw money, dates, pills, thumbnails, status and dropdowns on the canvas. The column picker offers static columns and dynamic ones (attributes, warehouses) loaded page by page; chosen columns persist to the staff member's metadata under grid_<name>.

nodes.name: Datagrid
nodes.summary: Canvas data grid with selection, row links, header icons, custom cell renderers, full-screen mode and an editable change tracker.

nodes.name: Custom grid cells
nodes.summary: Canvas renderers for money, discounted money, dates, numbers, pills, status, thumbnails, dropdowns and attribute types.

nodes.name: Column picker
nodes.summary: Lets a staff member choose static and dynamic columns, with search and pagination over attribute and warehouse columns.

nodes.name: Column persistence
nodes.summary: Saves the chosen grid columns as JSON in the staff member's metadata under grid_<name>, debounced by 500 ms, through accountUpdate.
nodes.detail: usePersistance reads the grid_<name> entry from the user's metadata into PersistedColumn objects, merges new column state, removes duplicates and saves through useMetadata, which runs accountUpdate and patches the cached user metadata directly. Parsing errors fall back to no persisted columns.

nodes.name: Conditional filters
nodes.summary: The expression filter bar on list pages: rows of field, condition and value that sync to the address bar and become GraphQL where or filter variables.
nodes.detail: The flow is UI, then value provider (address bar sync as a token array), then API providers (option lists and the state needed to rebuild filters from an address), then query builders. FiltersQueryBuilder resolves one query-variable builder per field and produces either the legacy filter input or the newer where input; the codebase is migrating to where. Constraints limit which fields can be combined, and per-entity initial state hooks reload the labels of values found in the address.

nodes.name: Conditional filters UI
nodes.summary: Renders the filter rows with their left operand, condition and value pickers and applies them on confirm.

nodes.name: Filter address-bar sync
nodes.summary: Reads and writes filter rows as query-string tokens so filtered lists can be bookmarked and shared.
nodes.detail: useUrlValueProvider parses the query string into a TokenArray, asks the API providers for the labels it needs, and rebuilds the FilterContainer once they load. Persisting writes the container back to the query string with qs.stringify while keeping navigation parameters such as pagination separate.

nodes.name: FiltersQueryBuilder
nodes.summary: Turns the filter container into GraphQL variables for the where or legacy filter input, pulling some keys such as channel to the top level.
nodes.detail: Each field is handled by a builder chosen by FilterQueryVarsBuilderResolver (33 builder classes for prices, dates, attributes, metadata, statuses and more). An optional AND wrapper avoids mixing operators with plain field filters.

nodes.name: Filter option providers
nodes.summary: Fetches option lists for filter values (channels, categories, collections, attributes, product types) and rebuilds filter labels from the address.
nodes.detail: Providers per list (products, orders, customers, vouchers and others) answer which left operands exist and which values each offers, using small _Search* queries. initialState hooks fetch the entities whose ids appear in the address so the filter rows show names instead of ids.

nodes.name: List search and filter bar
nodes.summary: The search input and filter area at the top of list pages, with a notice for legacy saved presets.

nodes.name: Forms and saving
nodes.summary: Form state, the sticky save bar, the leave-without-saving guard, metadata and rich text editors, and address and price fields.
nodes.detail: Detail pages wrap their inputs in Form (useForm keeps data and changed state), render a Savebar portal into the layout's anchor, and register with ExitFormDialogProvider, which blocks router navigation and browser unload while a form is dirty and asks before leaving.

nodes.name: Form and exit guard
nodes.summary: Form component and the provider that blocks navigation and page unload while a form has unsaved changes.

nodes.name: Save bar
nodes.summary: The sticky bottom bar with save, cancel and delete buttons, portalled into the layout anchor.

nodes.name: Metadata editor
nodes.summary: Card for editing public and private metadata key and value pairs on any entity.

nodes.name: Address form
nodes.summary: Address fields that load per-country validation rules from the API and show matching labels and choices.

nodes.name: Notifications
nodes.summary: Toast notifications built on Sonner, shown at the bottom right above the save bar, with a cap on visible toasts and a dismiss-all control.
nodes.detail: useNotifier is the hook every feature calls with status, title, text or apiMessage. NotificationProvider puts the callback in context; NotificationsToaster portals Sonner into #toast-portal and offsets it above the save bar when one is mounted. A queue limits visible toasts to three and keeps the rest waiting.

nodes.name: Toaster and queue
nodes.summary: Sonner toaster, toast component, dismiss-all pill and the queue that caps visible toasts at three.

nodes.name: useNotifier()
nodes.summary: Returns the notify callback; maps API messages and statuses to toast content and durations.

nodes.name: Dialogs and pickers
nodes.summary: The DashboardModal layout primitives and the assign dialogs for picking products, variants, categories, collections, warehouses and more.
nodes.detail: Assign dialogs share AssignContainerDialog (search, single or multi selection, infinite loading) and picker list states (loading, empty, backfill exhausted). Product and variant pickers add filters and select-all. Action and delete dialogs confirm destructive actions.

nodes.name: DashboardModal
nodes.summary: Modal root, content, header, actions, steps and picker header used by every dialog.

nodes.name: Assign dialog base
nodes.summary: Shared picker dialog with search and single or multiple selection used by category, collection, page and other assign dialogs.

nodes.name: Product picker
nodes.summary: Dialog to pick one or many products with filters, select-all and channel-aware rows.

nodes.name: Attributes card
nodes.summary: Renders attribute rows by input type, including reference lists and swatches, and fetches labels of referenced products and variants.

nodes.name: Channel availability card
nodes.summary: Per-channel publish, available-for-purchase and visibility settings with search and pagination over many channels.

nodes.name: List settings
nodes.summary: Per-list row count and column choices kept in localStorage, with one-time migrations for changed defaults.

nodes.name: Saved filter presets
nodes.summary: Save, update and delete named filter tabs for a list, kept in localStorage.

nodes.name: API error messages
nodes.summary: Maps each Saleor error code enum (account, app, order, product, webhook and others) to a translated message.
nodes.detail: One file per domain exports a function that takes an error fragment with a code enum and returns a message from react-intl, falling back to a common message. Views pass errors from mutation payloads through these to field helper texts and toasts.

nodes.name: Misc helpers
nodes.summary: extractMutationErrors, mutation status, transform helpers and other cross-cutting utilities.
nodes.detail: extractMutationErrors awaits a mutation promise and returns the errors array from its payload or GraphQL errors, which views use to decide whether to navigate. getMutationStatus turns a mutation result into a button state. utils/maps.ts maps connection edges to item lists, and url-utils parses and stringifies query strings.

nodes.name: GraphQL code generation
nodes.summary: GraphQL Code Generator configs for the main and staging schemas: types, hooks, fragment matchers and type policies.
nodes.detail: Documents are every queries.ts, mutations.ts, fragments file and searches hook; *.staging.ts files go only to the staging config. schema-directives.graphql declares @lockSchema so generation accepts it.

nodes.summary: Schema fetching, release and cleanup scripts, changeset and cloud-submodule checks, the message formatter and payment asset updates.

nodes.name: nginx config and runtime env rewrite
nodes.summary: Serves the single-page app with index.html fallback and no-cache HTML, and rewrites runtime config in index.html at container start.
nodes.detail: replace-env-vars.sh runs from the nginx entrypoint and uses sed to replace API_URL, APP_MOUNT_URI, EXTENSIONS_API_URL, CLOUD_API_URL, IS_CLOUD_INSTANCE and LOCALE_CODE inside window.__SALEOR_CONFIG__, so one image can point at different APIs. SALEOR_CLOUD_APP_DOMAIN and STATIC_URL are not rewritten.

nodes.summary: Heroku app manifest, Heroku static buildpack config and Netlify redirects, each routing every path to index.html.

nodes.name: Agent and contributor rules
nodes.summary: Conventions, which docs to read for which task, verification steps, changesets and analytics rules for contributors and coding agents.

nodes.name: Product glossary
nodes.summary: Dashboard terms whose names differ from the API (Model, Model type, navigation pins, warehouse and pickup terms).

nodes.summary: 0001 stores navigation pins in public metadata; 0002 keeps Saleor Cloud features in a private submodule loaded at build time.

nodes.name: Configuration guide
nodes.summary: Environment variables (API_URL, APP_MOUNT_URI, STATIC_URL, EXTENSIONS_API_URL, CLOUD_API_URL, deprecation banner) and schema fetching.

nodes.summary: How the dashboard builds against the main or staging schema with FF_USE_STAGING_SCHEMA and one Apollo client.

nodes.name: README
nodes.summary: Prerequisites (Node 24, pnpm, a running Saleor), development steps and optional named local addresses with portless.

nodes.name: Extensions section and addresses
nodes.summary: The /extensions routes and the address helpers that build app iframe, deep link and permission request addresses.
nodes.detail: ExtensionsSection routes explore, installed list, install from manifest (needs MANAGE_APPS), manifest app settings, permission requests, the app iframe view, plugin settings and custom app pages. Legacy /apps, /custom-apps and /plugins paths redirect here. resolveAppIframeUrl appends the dashboard's own query string and adds domain, saleorApiUrl and the app id so the app knows which API to call.

nodes.name: Installing apps
nodes.summary: Install an app from a manifest address: fetch and preview the manifest through the API, then start an asynchronous installation.
nodes.detail: The staff member pastes a manifest address (or arrives with ?manifestUrl=). appFetchManifest asks the API to download and validate the manifest, and the page shows the app's name, permissions and data privacy link, or which installed app already uses that identifier. Installing calls appInstall with the app name, manifest address and requested permissions; the returned installation id is added to the activeInstallations list in localStorage and the user is sent back to the installed list, which polls until the job finishes.

nodes.name: Installed and explore lists
nodes.summary: The installed apps and plugins list with pending installations and app problems, and the explore catalog from the marketplace or a bundled file.
nodes.detail: useInstalledExtensions merges installed apps and plugins; usePendingInstallation and useActiveAppsInstallations poll appsInstallations every 2 seconds while localStorage lists active installations, notify on success or failure, offer retry and removal, and refetch the extension list so new mount points appear. Explore loads categories from EXTENSIONS_API_URL or, when it is not set, the bundled extensions.json.

nodes.name: App settings, tokens and webhooks
nodes.summary: Manifest app details with activate, deactivate and delete, permission changes, custom apps with tokens and webhooks, and plugin settings.
nodes.detail: Manifest apps show about, permissions and webhook delivery status; an app can ask for more permissions, which lands on a page that shows the difference and calls appUpdate. Custom apps are created with appCreate (the token is shown once), get extra tokens with appTokenCreate and manage webhooks with subscription queries. Plugin pages edit global or per-channel plugin configuration. App problems and failed webhook deliveries surface as sidebar alerts.

nodes.name: App iframe and App Bridge
nodes.summary: Runs an app inside a sandboxed iframe and talks to it over postMessage using the App Bridge protocol from @saleor/app-sdk.
nodes.detail: AppFrame loads the app address with domain, saleorApiUrl, id, theme and feature flags in the query string. On load it posts a handshake event carrying the app's JSON Web Token (JWT) and the core and dashboard versions; until the handshake it shows a loader. A window message listener accepts only messages from the app's origin that look like App Bridge actions and dispatches them: notification, redirect, updateRouting, notifyReady, requestPermissions, formPayloadUpdate, popupClose, widgetResize, refreshEntity, openPopup and redirectToApp; each answer goes back as a response event. Theme, locale and token changes are pushed to the app, and the app token is refetched 30 seconds before it expires.

nodes.name: Extension mount points
nodes.summary: Where installed apps add menu items, buttons, widgets, popups, new-tab links, sidebar entries, search actions and home tabs inside the dashboard.
nodes.detail: Pages call useExtensions with their mount names; one ExtensionList query (first 100) returns the matching app extensions with their access tokens. Each becomes an object with an open function: NEW_TAB opens a GET link or posts a hidden form with the token and saleorApiUrl; POPUP opens the global AppDialog; APP_PAGE navigates to the app's deep route; WIDGET renders an AppFrame inline. A token-free snapshot in localStorage paints the structure before the query returns, and staff preferences can hide or pin extensions.

nodes.name: Apps GraphQL operations
nodes.summary: GraphQL queries and mutations for apps, installations, extensions, webhooks and plugins.
nodes.detail: These documents feed code generation, which turns them into the typed hooks the extension views call. The App fragment they share asks for accessToken, so app pages and extension lists always carry a current JSON Web Token (JWT) for the iframe. ExtensionList asks for at most 100 extensions filtered by mount name.

nodes.name: Extensions section routes
nodes.summary: The Switch for every /extensions page; only installing from a manifest is gated on MANAGE_APPS here.
nodes.detail: Manifest app pages resolve the address segment to an app id first with ResolveAppId, so links can use an app identifier as well as a GraphQL id. Plugin ids for the admin and customer email plugins redirect to the notification settings pages.

nodes.name: Extensions addresses
nodes.summary: Path constants and builders for extension pages, app deep links, permission requests and the app iframe address.
nodes.detail: ExtensionsPaths holds the /extensions route patterns; ExtensionsUrls builds concrete addresses: installed list, install with a manifestUrl query parameter, app settings, app deep links with an appPath, permission requests with redirectPath and requestedPermissions, and the iframe address.

nodes.name: ExtensionsUrls.resolveAppIframeUrl()
nodes.summary: Builds the iframe address: app address, then the dashboard's current query string, then domain, saleorApiUrl, id and extra parameters.
nodes.detail: domain (the API host) is deprecated in favour of saleorApiUrl but still sent.
nodes.signature: resolveAppIframeUrl(appId: string, appUrl: string, params) => string

nodes.name: Install from manifest page
nodes.summary: Form with the manifest address; after fetching shows the manifest preview, deprecation acknowledgement and the install button.

nodes.name: useFetchManifest()
nodes.summary: Calls appFetchManifest and, on a unique-identifier error, finds which installed app already uses it and links to it.
nodes.detail: It loads the first 100 installed apps to match by identifier or manifest address, so the error can say 'already installed' with a link to the app or its settings.

nodes.name: useInstallApp()
nodes.summary: Calls appInstall with the manifest's name and permissions, records the installation in localStorage and returns to the installed list.
nodes.detail: On success navigation runs twice, once in onCompleted and once after extractMutationErrors finds no errors; both push the same path.

nodes.name: Manifest and extension schemas
nodes.summary: Zod schemas for app manifests, extension targets (POPUP, NEW_TAB, APP_PAGE, WIDGET), mount names, options and permissions.
nodes.detail: Zod schemas parse values that come from the API or manifests before the dashboard uses them: mount names and targets are parsed when extensions load, options are validated before open(), and manifest fields drive the install preview. Invalid options make open() log an error instead of opening.

nodes.name: Installed extensions page
nodes.summary: Lists installed apps and plugins with pending installations, problems, deprecation and circuit-breaker badges, and filters.

nodes.name: Installation tracker
nodes.summary: Polls installation status every 2 seconds while localStorage lists active installations and reacts when each succeeds, fails or disappears.
nodes.detail: Pending installations found on the server but missing locally are added, so installs started elsewhere are tracked too. On success it notifies, refetches the app list and the ExtensionList query and tracks an analytics event; on failure it calls the error handler. Retry uses appRetryInstall and removal uses appDeleteFailedInstallation.

nodes.name: Explore extensions page
nodes.summary: Browse the extension catalog by category, see which are installed, and start an install or open the app.

nodes.name: Marketplace catalog loader

nodes.name: App problem alerts
nodes.summary: Sidebar dot and alert for apps with problems or failed webhook deliveries; dismissal state is saved in user metadata.

nodes.name: Manifest app settings
nodes.summary: App details with activate, deactivate and delete dialogs, permissions and webhook delivery status.

nodes.name: Permission request page

nodes.name: Custom app settings

nodes.name: Plugin settings

nodes.name: App page view

nodes.name: useAppActions()
nodes.summary: Listens for window messages from the app's origin, dispatches App Bridge actions to handlers and posts the response back.
nodes.detail: Messages without a type and payload.actionId (for example from browser extensions) are ignored. Unknown action types are reported to Sentry as a warning. Only the origin is checked, not which iframe sent the message.

nodes.summary: Sends an App Bridge event to the iframe's window with postMessage, targeting the app's origin only.

nodes.name: App token refresh
nodes.summary: Refetches the app (and so its token) 30 seconds before the JSON Web Token (JWT) expires, and again when a hidden tab becomes visible past that time.

nodes.name: Dashboard context updates

nodes.name: useExtensions()
nodes.summary: Queries extensions for a page's mount names, paints from a localStorage snapshot first, and builds open actions per target.
nodes.detail: Extensions with a relative address are dropped when their app has no appUrl. While data comes from the snapshot open does nothing, because the snapshot has no tokens. Loaded extensions are registered so an openPopup action can find a popup on the same page.

nodes.name: App popup provider
nodes.summary: Global holder for the one open popup extension: renders it in AppDialog with an AppFrame, or navigates for APP_PAGE targets.

nodes.name: New-tab extension actions

nodes.name: Widget extensions

nodes.name: Extension preferences

nodes.name: Search actions

nodes.detail: useSearchActions merges native actions with SEARCH_ACTION extensions whose options declare views and aliases, resolves which view the current page is and filters actions to the ones that match the typed text and context. Opening an app action runs the extension's open().

nodes.name: Extension registry
nodes.summary: Shares the extensions loaded on the current page so App Bridge openPopup can resolve a popup by identifier.
nodes.detail: A jotai atom maps each useExtensions caller to its extension list. The registration effect depends on a signature that includes the access token, because extensions first paint from cache with an empty token and the registry must pick up the real token when it arrives.

flows.name: A staff member signs in and the dashboard loads their permissions
flows.summary: From the email and password form to the permission-filtered sections, including token storage and refresh.

steps.text: A staff member opens the dashboard; with no stored refresh token the routes show the sign-in screen.
The sign-in view lists external providers from the shop and submits email and password through the user context.
handleLogin calls the auth SDK, then rejects users with no permissions or who are not staff by logging them out with an error.
login sends the tokenCreate mutation on the shared Apollo client and, on success, stores both tokens and marks the session authenticated.
The API checks the credentials and returns an access token, a refresh token and the user with permissions.
The access token stays in memory; the refresh token goes to localStorage so the next visit can sign in automatically.
UserDetails reads the user from the cache that login seeded, so no second request is needed; it carries userPermissions and accessible channels.
With authentication and a channel resolved, the routes render the layout and every section.
Each section route renders only when the user holds the PermissionEnum codes it lists, otherwise the not-found page.
Every later request carries the authorization-bearer token; within 120 seconds of expiry, or on an expired-signature error, one shared tokenRefresh renews it.

flows.name: An app is installed from the dashboard and opens inside it
flows.summary: From a manifest address to a running app iframe that talks to the dashboard through App Bridge.

steps.text: A staff member with MANAGE_APPS pastes a manifest address on the install page.
The page calls appFetchManifest so the API downloads and validates the manifest, then previews name and permissions.
The API fetches the manifest from the app and returns it, or an error such as an identifier already installed.
Install calls appInstall with the name, manifest address and permissions and records the installation id in localStorage.
The API creates an installation job and installs the app in the background.
The installed list polls appsInstallations every 2 seconds until the job succeeds or fails, then refetches apps and extensions.
Opening the app loads it with the App query, which includes its access token.
AppFrame renders the sandboxed iframe at the app address with saleorApiUrl, id, theme and flags, and posts a handshake with the token on load.
The app page runs inside the iframe and calls the GraphQL API with the token it received.
Messages from the app's origin are dispatched as App Bridge actions (notifications, redirects, permission requests) and answered with response events.

flows.name: An app adds a button and a widget to a dashboard page
flows.summary: How a page finds the extensions mounted on it and opens each target type.

steps.text: A page asks for its mount names; a token-free snapshot paints first while the ExtensionList query runs.
The API returns the matching extensions with their app, target and a fresh access token.
A NEW_TAB extension opens with GET, or posts a hidden form with accessToken, appId and saleorApiUrl.
A POPUP extension opens the global dialog with an AppFrame; an APP_PAGE extension navigates to the app's page.
WIDGET extensions render inline as auto-height frames on detail pages.
